name: Hover Card
summary: Supplemental destination preview with passive title and description anatomy, hover/focus interest, temporary Escape dismissal, and no essential-content or interaction ownership.

anatomy.name: root
anatomy.description: Inline wrapper that owns trigger-relative positioning.

anatomy.name: content
anatomy.description: Floating preview surface revealed by hover or focus-within.

anatomy.name: title
anatomy.description: Optional concise identity or preview title.

sizes.name: default
sizes.description: Default hover card content width and padding.

states.name: hover
states.description: Pointer hover state that reveals the preview surface.

states.name: focusWithin
states.description: Keyboard focus-within state that reveals the preview surface.

states.name: dismissed
states.description: Temporary target state that suppresses the surface after Escape until hover and focus leave the interest region.

behavior.name: visibility
behavior.description: The content is hidden by default and appears on pointer hover or keyboard focus within the root.

behavior.name: nonCriticalContent
behavior.description: Hover card content must be supplemental because it can be transient on touch, small screens, or targets without hover.

behavior.name: popoverFallback
behavior.description: Use Popover or Modal when the floating content contains required instructions, forms, destructive actions, or long interaction.

behavior.name: dismissal
behavior.description: Escape dismisses without moving focus; leaving the combined trigger/content interest region resets the temporary dismissed state.

behavior.name: destinationFallback
behavior.description: The trigger is a native link whose destination contains the complete information, so touch and assistive-technology users do not depend on the preview.

accessibility: Use a native link to a destination that contains the complete previewed information.
Reveal the preview on keyboard focus-within, not only on hover.
Keep the surface hoverable and persistent while pointer or focus remains in the combined interest region.
Support Escape dismissal without moving focus and reset dismissal after pointer/focus exit.
Keep important actions and required instructions outside the hover card.
Do not trap focus in a hover card.
Ensure content remains available through an alternative path on touch-first targets.

web.notes: Canonical CSS implements passive anatomy, pointer/focus visibility, dismissal state, content containment, and special media; target adapters own delay, Escape state coordination, and collision.
